They are distinguished by the vowels /əʊ/ and /ɔː/.
They differ in both quality and length of the vowel sound.
Teach-er contains two vowel sounds/beats.
Ed-u-ca-tion contains four syllables.
In the two-syllable noun 'table', the stress is on the first syllable.
In the two-syllable verb 'begin', the stress is on the second syllable.
The noun 'photograph' is stressed on the first syllable.
The word 'photography' shifts stress to the second syllable.
Words ending in '-ic' are usually stressed on the syllable immediately preceding the suffix.
'Cat' has only one vowel sound.
'Teacher' has two syllables (teach-er).
'Ba-na-na' contains three syllables.
'Ed-u-ca-tion' contains four syllables.
Primary stress is the strongest emphasis given to a syllable in a word.
Secondary stress is emphasis that is stronger than unstressed syllables but weaker than the primary stress.

questions.stem: Which word is stressed on second syllable?
questions.explanation: When used as a verb, 'record' is stressed on the second syllable.

questions.stem: Which word is stressed on first syllable?
questions.explanation: 'Table' is a noun and follows the general rule of first-syllable stress for two-syllable nouns.
Stress can change the meaning or grammatical category of a word (e.g., REcord vs reCORD).
As seen in many English heteronyms, stress position determines if a word is a noun or a verb.
Most two-syllable nouns in English carry stress on the first syllable.
Most two-syllable verbs in English carry stress on the second syllable.
'REcord' is the noun form, while 'reCORD' is the verb.
In the verb form 'to record', the stress is on the second syllable.
A syllable is a unit of pronunciation having one vowel sound, with or without surrounding consonants.
The nucleus of every syllable must be a vowel sound (or a syllabic consonant).
'Wa-ter' consists of two syllables.
'Ba-na-na' consists of three syllables.
'Ed-u-ca-tion' consists of four syllables.
In the International Phonetic Alphabet, primary stress is indicated by a high vertical mark.
Weak forms are pronunciations of words (like 'to' or 'and') that occur when they are not stressed.
Ourselves is the reflexive pronoun matching the plural subject We.
The strong form of a word is used when the word is emphasized or spoken in isolation.
Phonetics is the branch of linguistics that deals with the physical production and perception of speech sounds.

questions.stem: The following are necessary for developing effective study habits except .................
questions.explanation: Regular class avoidance hinders effective study habits, while attendance, time creation, and note review are beneficial.

questions.stem: In order to write a well-arranged paper, it is advisable to draft ...............
questions.explanation: An outline helps structure and organize a paper effectively before writing.

questions.stem: To avoid plagiarism, cited sources must be properly ....................
questions.explanation: Proper referencing gives credit to original authors and avoids plagiarism.

questions.stem: One specific use of language is for purposeful ......................
questions.explanation: Language is primarily used for purposeful communication between individuals.

questions.stem: Features of language include the following except ...................
questions.explanation: Language is creative and flexible, not strictly predictable in its use.

questions.stem: The rule-governed nature of language implies that words are not strung together ................
questions.explanation: Rule-governed language requires systematic arrangement, not random or haphazard order.

questions.stem: The ability of phonemes to cause change in meaning if substituted for each other is regarded as ..........
questions.explanation: Discreteness allows small sound units to create distinct meaning changes when substituted.

questions.stem: The role of language as it is used to sentence, acquit and wed people is referred to as ............... role.
questions.explanation: Performative language actually performs actions like sentencing or marrying when spoken.

questions.stem: Communication involves .......................... between two or more people.
questions.explanation: Communication fundamentally involves transmitting information between individuals.

questions.stem: The element of communication not readily required for the success of the communication process is .......................
questions.explanation: Noise is an obstacle, not a required element for successful communication.

questions.stem: Linguistic noise could be all of the following except ............... noise.
questions.explanation: Physical noise is environmental, not a type of linguistic noise.

questions.stem: The ................ confirms whether the message sent to the decoder is understood or not.
questions.explanation: Feedback from the receiver indicates whether the message was understood correctly.

questions.stem: .............. is the use of time in relation to interaction or communication.
questions.explanation: Chronemics specifically studies how time is used in communication.

questions.stem: The passing of information from the Manager to the clerks in an establishment is an example of the ............. pattern of communication.
questions.explanation: Communication flowing between different hierarchical levels is vertical communication.

questions.stem: English language is used in countries like the USA, UK and Canada as a ...............
questions.explanation: English is the native or first language for most citizens of the USA, UK, and Canada.

questions.stem: Physical appearance can be taken as a form of ............... communication.
questions.explanation: Physical appearance conveys messages without words, making it non-verbal communication.

questions.stem: In 'The women are going to come late', women is an example of ................ noun.
questions.explanation: Women is a general name for a class of people, not a specific person or place.

questions.stem: In 'Justice got served at last', ............... is the abstract noun contained in the sentence.
questions.explanation: Justice is an abstract noun representing a concept or quality without physical form.

questions.stem: The tournament would be played in the different .............. across the federation.
questions.explanation: Stadia is the correct plural form of stadium in standard English.

questions.stem: The nun had ........... car fixed at the nearby garage.
questions.explanation: Nun refers to a female religious person, so the possessive pronoun her is correct.

questions.stem: That is the man ........... drove the bus.
questions.explanation: Who is the correct relative pronoun referring to a person (the man) as the subject.

questions.stem: Of all the students in the class she is the ................
questions.explanation: Superlative degree 'most brilliant' is correct when comparing three or more students.

questions.stem: The modal auxiliary in 'We could be late if we don't start out soon' is ...............
questions.explanation: Could is a modal auxiliary verb expressing possibility.

questions.stem: The object of the verb in 'The boy broke the existing record' is .............
questions.explanation: The existing record receives the action of the verb broke, making it the object.

options.C: verbs forming their past forms without 'ed'

questions.explanation: Irregular verbs change form internally rather than adding -ed for past tense.

questions.stem: In 'The man died', 'died' is used as a/an ................. verb.
questions.explanation: Died does not take a direct object, making it an intransitive verb.

questions.stem: 'To meet' in 'We meet to part and we part to meet' is an example of ............. verb.
questions.explanation: The infinitive 'to meet' does not show tense or agreement, making it non-finite.

questions.stem: The winner came from behind to breast the tape. 'from behind' as used exemplifies .........
questions.explanation: From behind consists of two prepositions functioning together as a compound preposition.

questions.stem: In 'He would not continue the class unless the culprit is found', 'unless' functions as a ........
questions.explanation: Unless introduces a subordinate clause showing condition.

questions.stem: A compound sentence features two .............. clauses.
questions.explanation: A compound sentence joins two independent clauses with a coordinating conjunction.

questions.stem: 'While it was raining' as used in 'She took her rest while it was raining' exemplifies a ..........
questions.explanation: While it was raining cannot stand alone and depends on the main clause for meaning.

questions.stem: In 'the aspirants are called for a consensus meeting', the subject of the verb is ............
questions.explanation: The aspirants performs the action of being called, making it the subject.

questions.stem: 'the man in blue shirt' in 'It was given to the man in blue shirt' exemplifies a ................
questions.explanation: The entire phrase functions as a noun receiving the action of the verb.

questions.stem: 'the book' in 'She gave the book to John' functions as a ....................
questions.explanation: The book receives the action of the verb gave directly.

questions.stem: Bread and butter ...... good for breakfast.
questions.explanation: Bread and butter as a combined concept takes a singular verb is.

questions.stem: The rule of the game says 'everyman for .............'
questions.explanation: Everyman is singular and masculine, requiring the reflexive pronoun himself.
Seat is the correct noun meaning a place to sit.

questions.stem: The police ......... blamed for the security breach.
questions.explanation: Police is a collective noun usually taking plural verb were in this context.

questions.stem: Listening is different from hearing because ............................
questions.explanation: Listening is an active, conscious process requiring attention, unlike passive hearing.

questions.stem: Worry, hunger and discomfort can ........... effective listening.
questions.explanation: These factors create barriers that hinder or impede effective listening.

questions.stem: A passive listener will .................... from a lecture.
questions.explanation: Passive listening without engagement results in minimal information retention.

questions.stem: Speaking, as a skill, differs from ordinary conversation because it ...............
questions.explanation: Effective speaking as a skill involves deliberate preparation and organization.

questions.stem: A speaker's posture, diction as well as ........ are important for a successful delivery.
questions.explanation: Physical appearance affects audience perception and speaker credibility.

questions.stem: Skimming and scanning are samples of ............ reading speeds.
questions.explanation: Skimming and scanning are fast reading techniques used in extensive reading.

questions.stem: Head movement, regression and vocalization are .............. for effective reading.
questions.explanation: These habits are harmful or inimical to efficient reading.

questions.stem: Factors that can aid the reader's comprehension include intelligence, state of mind and .......
questions.explanation: Interest in the material enhances comprehension and engagement.

questions.stem: The phoneme common to boy, toy and joy is ...........
questions.explanation: All three words contain the same diphthong vowel sound /ɔɪ/.

questions.stem: Thanks and thought begins with the ...... phoneme.
questions.explanation: Both words begin with the voiceless dental fricative sound /θ/.

questions.stem: Coherence, as a feature of a good paragraph, implies that the ideas in the paragraph should be ......
questions.explanation: Coherence requires that all ideas in a paragraph logically relate to each other.

questions.stem: A paragraph is a collection of ...........
questions.explanation: A paragraph consists of multiple sentences developing a single idea.

questions.stem: When a letter ends with 'Yours faithfully' as closing complimentary remarks, it is a .......... letter.
questions.explanation: Yours faithfully is a standard formal closing when the recipient's name is unknown.

questions.stem: 'will you go by plane' is best punctuated correctly as .............
questions.explanation: The sentence is a question requiring capital W and a question mark.

questions.stem: Each man gave ........... best at the meeting.
questions.explanation: Each man is singular masculine, requiring the possessive pronoun his.

questions.stem: Neither Grace nor Mike .......... the answers to the riddles.
questions.explanation: With neither/nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject Mike, singular.

questions.stem: He ........ the first train but we get the second train every day.
questions.explanation: The present tense gets agrees with the singular subject He.

questions.stem: A phrase is different from a clause in that it ........................
questions.explanation: A phrase lacks a finite verb, while a clause contains one.

questions.stem: The underlined part in 'The big house was built in a very short time' is an example of .......
questions.explanation: In a very short time modifies the verb was built, functioning as an adverb.

questions.stem: In 'They made Frank the captain', 'the captain' functions as ....................
questions.explanation: The captain completes the meaning of the direct object Frank.

questions.stem: Because of the poor network, the many dialed calls were not ...............
questions.explanation: Going through means successfully connecting in telecommunications.
The tag question for a positive statement with is uses isn't it.

questions.stem: We were feeling cold when the plane landed. ....................
questions.explanation: The tag question for we were positive uses weren't we.
Could you please is a polite request form for asking a favor.

questions.stem: The five apples are to be shared ................ the three boys.
questions.explanation: Among is used for sharing when more than two entities are involved.

questions.stem: All the ............... will be expected to attend as well.
questions.explanation: Staff is a collective noun that remains unchanged in the plural.
Its is the correct possessive pronoun for a non-living thing like monument.

questions.stem: The men are ready to do the clearing ..................
questions.explanation: Themselves is the correct reflexive pronoun for the plural subject the men.
